about: Own-words reads from the daily research task (ADMIS, Rabobank, Czapp and the news feed). fund_score: -1 bearish to +1 bullish, a judgement on the fundamental news only.

corn.fundamental: Corn fought back from overnight losses to close higher into the Thanksgiving break, following soybeans and a softer dollar. Slow US export pace is still the main drag; no new demand news.
events: Corn rallying into Thanksgiving break (Barchart)
Corn and soybeans close higher, livestock fall (Successful Farming)
Corn exports lag into the holiday (Barchart)

soybeans.fundamental: CBOT is closed today. Wednesday's late rally was helped by talk of firmer Chinese buying, but longer-run Chinese import growth is slowing, which caps how much US export demand can recover; the record October NOPA crush keeps domestic use strong.
events: Corn and soybeans rally as China boosts demand (AgroLatam)
Slowing Chinese soybean demand growth challenges exporters (Czapp)
NOPA reports record October crush (Brownfield)

meal.fundamental: A record October NOPA crush shows plants running flat out for meal, which adds supply but also confirms strong demand; Jan closed ~358 (+2%) on technical buying before the holiday.
events: NOPA reports record October soybean crush (Brownfield)
Corn, soybeans and meal rally pre-holiday on technical buying (AgWeb)

oil.fundamental: The record October NOPA crush means more soyoil coming onto an already heavy market, keeping Jan (~58.3) pinned near its nine-month low; firmer crude in holiday trade is the only help.
events: NOPA reports record October soybean crush (Brownfield)
Soy oil at nine-month low as crush runs hard (Bloomberg)

wheat.fundamental: Wheat was mixed into the holiday; the outlook for more harvested HRW acres in southwest Kansas and improving ratings keep exportable supply ample.
events: Wheat posts mixed trade on Wednesday (Barchart)
SW Kansas farmer sees more harvested wheat acres ahead (Brownfield)
Canada forecast to rank second in wheat exports (World Grain)

kc.fundamental: KC tracked Chicago in mixed trade; expectations of more harvested acres in southwest Kansas add to the comfortable 2027 HRW supply view.
events: SW Kansas farmer sees more harvested wheat acres ahead (Brownfield)
Wheat mixed on Wednesday (Barchart)

cotton.fundamental: Mar rallied into the close to ~82.9, clearing Tuesday's highs and the 82.7 resistance as a weaker dollar and firmer crude helped outside money back in. No new supply or demand data; old-crop Mar/May keeps leaning on Texas Plains losses, but high-grade certs stay a two-sided risk for longs.
events: Mar ~82.9, through 82.7 resistance (ICE)
Dollar index slips, firmer crude (WSJ, Pro Farmer)
Tuesday gains on outside factors (Barchart)

hogs.fundamental: Dec hogs settled ~49.9 (-3.6%), another 52-week low, as weak pork demand and Dec liquidation continue; lower frozen pork stocks are not helping yet. CME is closed today.
events: Cattle, hog futures lower ahead of holiday (Brownfield)
Lean hogs fall to new lows on weak pork demand (The Pig Site)

cattle.fundamental: Live cattle broke sharply into the close on Wednesday with no cash trade established; Dec settled near 223.6 (-1%), just above the 222.2 support. Supplies are still tight, so this looks like position-squaring before the holiday rather than a change in fundamentals; CME is closed today.
events: Cattle crash pre-holiday (AgWeb, Barchart)
Cattle, hog futures lower ahead of Thursday holiday (Brownfield)

feeders.fundamental: Jan feeders fell 1.6% to ~327.4, now close to the 325 support and still below the 50-day average. The closed Mexican border keeps feeder supply tight and screwworm stays the tail risk.
events: Cattle crash pre-holiday (AgWeb, Barchart)
Cattle, hog futures lower ahead of Thursday holiday (Brownfield)

class3.fundamental: CME cheese blocks led a slightly firmer dairy complex ahead of the holiday, but milk output growth near 2% y/y still caps Class III upside.
events: Dairy prices slightly higher before Thanksgiving, cheese blocks lead (Brownfield)
Dairy heads into 2027 with growing demand and concerns (Dairy Herd)

class4.fundamental: Dairy products edged higher before the holiday, a small steadying after Tuesday's 7-cent drop in spot nonfat dry milk; powder demand is still the question for Class IV.
events: Dairy prices slightly higher before Thanksgiving (Brownfield)
Nonfat dry milk drops 7 cents at CME (Brownfield)

palm.fundamental: India is turning back to palm after China's cheap soyoil exports cooled, a modest demand offset to China halting palm purchases. It does not change the picture of Malaysian stocks well above average, and weaker crude still narrows the biodiesel pull.
events: China soyoil export boom cools as India turns to palm (Bloomberg)
China halts palm oil purchases as storage fills (Bloomberg)

natgas.fundamental: Jan is down about 1% to ~3.62 in holiday trade as a mild Thanksgiving outlook erodes Northeast cash premiums; the bullish storage print and record LNG feedgas are being offset by weather and strong output.
events: Mild Thanksgiving outlook cuts Northeast cash premiums (NGI)
US LNG feedgas near record 21.5 Bcf/d (NGI)

crude.fundamental: WTI Jan is up ~1.2% to ~84.7 and Brent ~91.3 in thin holiday trade, as Middle East risk after the Houthi strike on a Saudi refinery stays priced in. OPEC+ capacity disputes (Kazakhstan, Iraq) still point to more supply later.
events: Oil futures pick up as Middle East tensions persist (WSJ)
Kazakhstan joins Iraq pushing OPEC for higher capacity rating (OilPrice.com)

ulsd.fundamental: ULSD Jan is ~3.68 (+0.6%) with crude; a recent slump in diesel cracks gives a brief easing of the squeeze, but distillate stocks are still below average and the Saudi refinery attack keeps risk in the price.
events: Diesel's slump offers brief respite from energy turmoil (Bloomberg)
Cheaper gasoline won't fix the diesel squeeze (OilPrice.com)

rbob.fundamental: RBOB is little changed near ~2.43; cheaper gasoline and stocks above average in the low-demand season keep the crack weak relative to diesel.
events: Cheaper gasoline won't fix the diesel squeeze (OilPrice.com)
US gasoline stocks hold steady (OilPrice.com)
